margin_framing.metric_basis_note: DXC frames margin as adjusted EBIT margin (non-GAAP; VA operating_income equals company adjusted EBIT, FY2026 $970M = 10-K). Target and consensus are compared on that same adjusted EBIT basis. The stage 1 screen and the quant fields use EBITDA margin.
margin_framing.synergy_year: FY2029 (three-year plan horizon); stated as a $1B to $1.5B range of reduced spending, midpoint recorded, not all drops to margin

statements.quote: With this improved revenue performance, combined with our customer zero strategy of deploying AI capability internally, we're going to drive margin improvement from our current guidance for fiscal 2027, which is 6%-7%, to an acceleration of 8%-10% within the plan horizon.
statements.speaker: Rob Del Bene

statements.quote: Through these efforts, we're targeting reduced spending in the range of $1 billion-$1.5 billion with Agentic productivity improvements in our delivery operations and in our support organizations.
statements.speaker: Rob Del Bene

statements.quote: We outlined a disciplined financial framework through fiscal year 2029, including a return to organic growth, non-GAAP EBIT margin expansion, and continued strong free cash flow generation.
statements.speaker: Raul Fernandez

statements.quote: We continue to anticipate adjusted EBIT margin for the full year in the range of 6%-7%, with margins improving sequentially throughout the year, supported by cost management, operational efficiencies, and improving revenue profile in the second half of the year.
statements.speaker: Rob Del Bene
statements.doc_title: DXC Technology Co Q1 2027 Earnings Call

street.gap_assumption: Baba FY labels follow DXC fiscal years ending March (FY2029 = April 2028 to March 2029). Compares the 9.0% midpoint of the 8% to 10% adjusted EBIT target with FY2029 consensus adjusted EBIT margin of 7.71% ($879.8M on $12,061.6M revenue). Against the 8% low end the gap is 29 bps. FY2029 consensus EBITDA margin is 14.40%; FY2026 is reported actual.
street.source: Baba data_financials consensus (summary and fundamentals, Visible Alpha)

evidence_of_progress.note: Q4 FY2026 adjusted EBIT margin 7.57% vs 7.26% (VA, +31 bps). Q1 FY2027 adjusted EBIT margin 5.0%, down 180 bps (Del Bene, doc 112121). Organic revenue fell 6.7% in Q1; FY2027 guide is 6% to 7% adjusted EBIT, below the 7.7% of FY2026, so the plan starts from a step down. Q2 FY2027 guide about 6%.

verdict: Closest structural match so far: deeply cheap, a CFO-stated 8% to 10% FY2029 adjusted EBIT target the street models at 7.7%, and an external operating President, but the CEO is not new and margins are still falling.
open_questions: Is Paul Taylor a CEO successor? His remit covers all operations and profitability, and Fernandez's contract runs to 2028-03-31.
How much of the $1B to $1.5B spending reduction reaches margin versus being reinvested or passed through in AI-driven price competition?
The prior FY2024 outlook of 10% to 11% adjusted EBIT margin (cited by an analyst on the Q1 FY2023 call, doc 91623) ended at 7.4% (VA FY2024). What makes this plan more credible?
